proof.text: Use HenselianLocalRing.TFAE to obtain lifting of simple roots of monic polynomials from the henselian local ring instance. This is exactly the root-lifting hypothesis of lem-weil-pbc-root-lifting-etale-retraction.

Convert the ideal residue-field hypothesis to the scheme residue-field hypothesis. Put x=q' and y=Spec(phi)(x). The affine residue-field isomorphisms give maps beta:B→kappa(x) and alpha:S→kappa(y). Naturality of global evaluation gives beta composed with phi equal to the scheme residue-field map composed with alpha. The composite S→kappa(q') is surjective: it is the given bijective ideal residue-field map composed with the surjective map S→kappa(m). Transport through the affine residue-field isomorphism makes beta composed with phi surjective. Therefore the scheme residue-field map is surjective; it is injective as a homomorphism of fields.

Apply lem-weil-pbc-root-lifting-etale-retraction with this root-lifting property and the converted residue-field bijectivity. Forget the uniqueness part to obtain the requested algebra homomorphism with maximal-ideal preimage q'.

blueprint_update.statement: Let $(S,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], let $\varphi:S\to B$ be a ring map such that $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ is etale, and let $\mathfrak q'\subset B$ be a prime ideal with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q')=\mathfrak m$ such that the induced map of residue fields $\kappa\to\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ is bijective. Then there exists an $S$-algebra homomorphism $\sigma:B\to S$ with $\sigma^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak q'$.

proof.text: Since $S$ is henselian, every monic polynomial over $S$ whose reduction modulo $\mathfrak m$ has a simple root in $\kappa$ has a root in $S$ lifting it (one of the standard equivalent characterizations of henselian local rings). This is exactly the root-lifting hypothesis of the root-lifting retraction lemma.

Let $x=\mathfrak q'\in\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $y=\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{Spec}S$ its image. The residue field of the scheme $\operatorname{Spec}B$ at $x$ is $\kappa(\mathfrak q')$, and that of $\operatorname{Spec}S$ at $y$ is $\kappa$, compatibly with the maps $B\to\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ and $S\to\kappa$, and the residue-field map of $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ at $x$ is the given map $\kappa\to\kappa(\mathfrak q')$. The composite $S\to\kappa\to\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ is surjective, as a surjection followed by a bijection; so the residue-field map of $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ at $x$ is surjective, and it is injective as a homomorphism of fields. Thus the residue-field hypothesis of that lemma holds.

Apply the root-lifting retraction lemma with this root-lifting property and this residue-field bijectivity. Forget the uniqueness part to obtain the requested algebra homomorphism with maximal-ideal preimage q'. ([lem-weil-pbc-root-lifting-etale-retraction]).
